title: Instructions passed by tell are acted on, not answered

requirements.text: Every genlock tell carries an explicit kind, either do (start work) or ask (answer only), and the Subassistant forwards that kind unchanged
requirements.check: file: the forwarded message to the session shows the same kind the Assistant sent, in tests covering both kinds

requirements.text: A session receiving a do message replies starting with STARTED or NOT STARTED and a reason, and genlock flags a reply that has neither
requirements.check: manual: send a do message; the relay shows STARTED or NOT STARTED, and a reply with neither is flagged to the Assistant

text: Investigated: the do-message never reached the ice cream session. Tally's 02:07Z tell (1117 bytes) reached nightmaremode's Subassistant as only its last 95 bytes ('k, and report back...'); Subassistant asked what was meant, and that question never reached Tally (it told nobody, so nothing relayed back). The 'No...' at 03:25Z answered TJ's own direct question 'did you build...'. Every tell over ~1 KB is cut (22:36Z too); all <=804 arrived whole. Proposal sent to TJ; nothing built.
The 1 KB cut is in how the session reads an unbracketed burst arriving in 1024-byte pieces (a raw-mode PTY passed 3000 bytes intact in a test)
breaks: If the cut is elsewhere (SwiftTerm or the host), bracketed paste will not fix it; the >1KB delivery test catches that

text: Build all three: paste-mode delivery with a transcript check and one retry, then do/ask kinds with STARTED/NOT STARTED. The 'dead end at the Subassistant' step is dropped: the 02:07 question was relayed (Tally 02:08:16) but cut in delivery, same cause; the Stop hook already relays a Subassistant reply that told nobody (tests/run.mjs:910)
user_said: i think this explains the bugs i was seeing. yea lets build this. these are very good additions.

text: A message the app types into a session (a tell, a relay report, a phone message) arrives whole: 3 KB typed as the app types it shows up in that session's transcript as exactly what was sent
check: manual: scratchpad claudeprobe.py against real Claude Code: plain typing splits 3 KB into 3 pieces; paste mode arrives whole in 1; then the app's own path delivers a >1 KB tell whole

text: The app checks each typed message reached the session's transcript; if not, it types it once more, and if that fails too, the sender hears it was not delivered
check: file: app/Tests/GenlockCoreTests: the transcript matcher finds a whole message, misses a cut one, and ignores paste wrappers and line breaks; the briefing names an undelivered message

evidence: tests/run.mjs 577/577: tell without a kind refuses and writes nothing; --do text starts '[do] please run it. This is an instruction...' with awaiting kind do; --ask text '[ask] ... do not start work on it.' kind ask; Tally->Subassistant message carries '[do] run done' + 'genlock tell --do', sub awaiting kind do; Subassistant passing it as --ask is refused ('pass it on as --do'), as --do passes with kind do

swift test 140/140; DeliveryTests 5/5: whole message found through <pasted_content> wrappers split in 3 and line breaks, and as content parts; tail-only ('k, and report back.') and an assistant quoting it are not delivered; verdicts wait(grace/working)->retype->lost, lost after 30 min regardless; reportUndelivered writes an 'undelivered' relay to the asking Subassistant, clears awaiting and its owed marker; briefing says 'never received a message'

text: Built: TerminalSession.submit types as a paste (Claude Code enables ?2004h, checked) and checks the transcript, retyping once when idle, then an 'undelivered' relay to the sender; tell --do/--ask required, carried through the Subassistant (a different kind refused), Stop hook flags a do reply without STARTED/NOT STARTED (ack none) and the briefing warns Tally. Rules updated. CLI 577/577, app 140/140, app installed NOT relaunched. Left: req 2 and 3 live checks after relaunch. Uncommitted.
The live CLI now refuses a tell without --do/--ask, while the running app's Tally rule predates it; the refusal names the fix, so Tally retries
breaks: If Tally does not retry, its tells fail until the app is relaunched

evidence: Live, through the relaunched app (built 07:44:03, running since 07:44:06): a 1788-byte [do] tell dropped into probe session 6E681F38's channel arrived in its transcript 6b836bcc as 1 paste block, whole (squeezed match), and the reply quoted both ALPHA-START and OMEGA-END. Earlier probe: plain typing split 3 KB into 3 pieces; paste mode whole

Live: the probe's reply opened 'STARTED: echo PROBE-OK printed PROBE-OK...' and its relay-1794499044666 carries ack:'started'; a separate real session also replied 'STARTED. I've released my hold...'. A reply saying neither gets ack 'none' and the briefing 'WITHOUT saying whether it started' (tests/run.mjs + DeliveryTests)

answers.observed: probe transcript 6b836bcc: 1788-byte prompt whole in 1 paste block; reply 'STARTED: ...ALPHA-START...OMEGA-END'; relay ack started; scratch probe 3 KB plain -> 3 pieces, paste -> 1 whole
answers.cause: measured, not hypothesised: plain typing is split at ~1 KB by Claude Code (seen); the earlier total loss of the front pieces was not reproduced, only the split
answers.absence: the transcript check reads only the last 4 MB of the transcript and only user prompts; a message missing there after a 4 MB turn would be retyped (bounded to one retry)
answers.assumption: mine: Claude Code always enables bracketed paste once its prompt is up; a message typed before then goes as plain keys, and the transcript check catches it
answers.falsify: a tell over 1 KB that reaches a session cut, or a do reply without STARTED/NOT STARTED that reaches Tally unflagged
